summary: TEN OF THE FOURTEEN CLAIMS REPRODUCE EXACTLY, INCLUDING EVERY NUMBER IN THE O11 LADDER AND EVERY COMMIT IN THE 37-TREE K15 SWEEP. THREE ARE REFUTED, AND ONE OF THE THREE IS THE ROUND'S RESULT. (1) RULE 5 MISSES A LIVE INSTANCE OF THE VERY CLASS IT WAS WRITTEN FOR. src/opt/api.py:1930 builds Gate('opt.lr.shift_warm', False, shift_warm, '> 0', reachable=False, reason='OPT_LR_SHIFT_WARM=0, the shipped default ...') on `elif shift_warm <= 0:`. There is no refusal and no clamp on that lever -- `shift_warm = int(opt.lr_shift_warm)` at :1551 -- and I built OPT with OPT_LR_SHIFT_WARM=-3 and rendered the line: `Gate opt.lr.shift_warm: UNREACHABLE (-3 vs > 0) -- OPT_LR_SHIFT_WARM=0, the shipped default and the setting every recorded result was produced under.` That is the ckpt.periodic_armed defect, verbatim in shape, standing on the tree. Rule 5 does not see it for ONE reason: `ranged` is set only when the Gate sits on the ELSE of the ordering test, and this Gate sits on the BODY of `shift_warm <= 0`. Deleting `and in_else` catches it, reports NOTHING ELSE on any of the 37 trees, and leaves all 59 K15 self-test cases green. The same narrowing means the historical ckpt defect, rewritten as `elif every <= 0:` with the gate in the body -- an identical program -- passes K15 with the literal restored; I planted exactly that and got PASS. (2) FINDING 13 IS REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT: stripping the `bool(...)` wrapper does NOT 'gain NOTHING on any of the 37 trees'. It takes rule 4's coverage from 9 of 15 to 13 of 15 at nine of the thirteen gate-bearing trees, f11ae02 and the working tree included, because four of the six residual gates write `reachable=bool(X)` against a reason branching on `X`. Two lines add it, the suite stays green and rule 4 still fires zero times on all 37 trees. The shipped file's stated reason for leaving the residue -- 'a reason branching on a SECOND NAME for the same condition ... deciding those are the same condition is inference' -- is false for four of the six. (3) THE GREEN O11 CASE EXERCISES ONE EXEMPTION, NOT TWO: deleting the src/spine/derive.py exemption alone leaves O11 PASS at 166 sites and all 32 cases green, so that half is a guard nothing has ever tripped. (4) THE FILED O13-WIDENING REMEDY CANNOT REACH ITS OWN SUCCESS CRITERION: implemented exactly as written it leaves SEVEN findings in tests/test_ownership.py, not zero, six of them in prose this round wrote.

findings.detail: HALF THE CLAIM HOLDS AND HALF DOES NOT. The assemble.py half is exactly as filed: exempting only derive.py turns 'O11: the named conversion, derive's own arithmetic and a coupling compute are ADMITTED' into 'O11 failed a tree it must pass', naming src/spine/assemble.py:2 inside the synthetic COUPLINGS compute. The derive.py half is not: exempting only assemble.py leaves O11 PASS at 166 arithmetic sites and all 32 self-test cases green, on the live tree AND on the case tree. The reason is that _CLOCK_DERIVE's body is `units.Windows(int(rate) * int(count))`, whose operands are Calls over PARAMETERS and carry no clock-lever Attribute at all -- and the same is true of the real src/spine/derive.py, whose 15 extra BinOp sites produce zero findings when the exemption is removed. So the derive.py exemption is a guard nothing in the suite has ever tripped and nothing on the tree needs, which is the exact shape ('60 of the survey's 475 records are guards whose condition could not be satisfied') the rest of this file cites as the thing to avoid. It is defensible to KEEP it as a declared design position; it is not defensible to report it as exercised.
